audit.why: Packet chart gives Akali all seven rows and the content layer agrees; 49.66% over 731 games. Taliyah has no duel pattern, only terrain and range, so the difficulty comes from her disengage rather than from losing trades.
audit.corrected: Difficulty stays 7/10 — the lane is hard to close, not hard to win.

audit.why: Weaver's Wall is 180/150/120s with no damage — the level 6 text is right that it does not change the lane. Akali's real spikes are level 3 shroud and first item; Taliyah's is Threaded Volley falling from 7s to 3s, which is what makes her unkillable late if you have not closed.
audit.corrected: Kept the level 6 framing, added Threaded Volley's cooldown decay to the cooldown section.
sources: brief enemyKit Q cd 7/6/5/4/3, R cd 180/150/120

audit.whatIsWrong: Unraveled Earth is called an 'E root' in six places. It is not a root.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Taliyah creates a slowing minefield. If enemies dash through it or are knocked through it, the mines explode and stun them.' Against Akali that is the single most important interaction in the matchup — her E recast dash and both casts of Perfect Execution detonate the mines and stun her, and Seismic Shove exists to knock her through them for the same result. Walking in on foot takes only the slow. Nothing in the current text says any of this.
audit.corrected: Enter on foot, keep E's recast for the exit, and never aim R through her minefield. Unraveled Earth is a flat 14s at every rank; Seismic Shove is 14s at rank 1 down to 8s.
sources: brief enemyKit E text and cd 14

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Both of her setup spells are on 14s at the relevant ranks, which is a genuinely long punish window.
audit.corrected: Unraveled Earth 14s flat, Seismic Shove 14s at rank 1, Threaded Volley 7s falling to 3s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed: full layer read Taliyah/Taliyah/Taliyah/Taliyah/Skill/Skill/Skill while content and the packet both read Akali on all seven rows.
audit.why: Two layers answering 'who wins Level 1' differently on the same page.
audit.corrected: Flip all seven full-layer sides to Akali.

audit.why: The kit file's derived flags mark grounding on Threaded Volley and Seismic Shove, but Riot's descriptions for both mention no grounding. Per the rule I trusted the description and asserted no grounding anywhere in the text.

edits.before: He pokes until you shroud, then the lane belongs to the smoke — trade in obscured windows and energy-walk the rest.
edits.after: She pokes at 1000 range until you shroud, then the lane belongs to the smoke — the danger is her minefield, not her poke.

edits.before: Survive the poke, then win every shrouded exchange until one becomes a kill. Keep one eye on Seismic Shove and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Survive the poke, then win every shrouded exchange until one becomes a kill. Never dash through her minefield — walk in, and dash only on the way out.

edits.before: Taliyah wins by landing Seismic Shove, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Taliyah wins by shoving you into Unraveled Earth, stunning you mid-dash, then kiting the rest of the lane at 1000 range.

edits.before: Q the wave edge and his toes — the energy crunch is real, so every kama needs to farm AND poke at once.
edits.after: Q the wave edge and her toes — Threaded Volley is 7s at rank 1, so step in the moment she spends it on the wave.

edits.before: Shroud online: the trade pattern is Q-auto, shroud the answer, Q again from the smoke. Most mids lose this exchange.
edits.after: Shroud is online and Seismic Shove is her only answer — bait the throw, shroud where you land, and trade out of the smoke.

edits.before: Passive-weave every trade: spell, walk out of the ring, auto the edge — the energy refunds pay the whole lane.
edits.after: Unraveled Earth is up now: a flat 14s minefield that stuns anything dashing through, so trade on foot, never on E.

edits.before: Perfect Execution online — the double-dash R turns half-health mages into clean-up duty. Look for the all-in.
edits.after: Perfect Execution online, but both casts are dashes — never aim them through her mines. Execute from clean ground.

edits.before: - Taliyah Seismic Shove: matchup-defining — The shove into Unraveled Earth is her whole setup — sidestep it and the burst whiffs. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Twilight Shroud has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Unraveled Earth is a flat 14s and only stuns what dashes or is knocked through it — your E recast and both R casts set it off. - Seismic Shove is 14s at rank 1 and exists to throw you into that minefield. - Walk in, dash out. - Threaded Volley drops to 3s by rank 5.

edits.before: If Taliyah gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Seismic Shove extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q range and stay relevant through shroud picks.
edits.after: If Taliyah gets a kill she simply kites — contest her worked ground and stop dashing into mines. Two kills: farm at 550, fight only while Seismic Shove is down, and stay relevant through shroud picks.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Taliyah has no duel combo, only terrain — walk through the minefield instead of dashing it, then E-reset out with the kill.

edits.before: Ahead, erase the lane: shroud every contact, all-in the whiffs, and roam with R banked — fed Akali turns mid into a no-cast zone for Taliyah.
edits.after: Ahead, deny her the terrain: contest worked ground, all-in inside Seismic Shove's 14 seconds, and keep R for the kill, not for the chase.

edits.before: The shove into Unraveled Earth is her whole setup — sidestep it and the burst whiffs. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: The shove into Unraveled Earth is her whole setup — the mines only stun dashes, so enter on foot and save E's recast for the exit.

edits.before: Taliyah burns Seismic Shove on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Taliyah burns Seismic Shove on nothing — that is 14 seconds without her setup.

edits.before: You beat her early since her worked-ground setup and root cooldown make her vulnerable to your all-in before she's online
edits.after: You beat her early since worked ground is slow to build and her minefield only punishes the dashes you can decline to take

edits.before: Taliyah's worked ground Q needs setup time and her E root has a long cooldown early, so you can all-in through her poke before she has enough mana or worked-ground uptime to threaten back.
edits.after: Taliyah's worked ground needs setup time and Unraveled Earth is a flat 14s that only stuns dashes, so you can all-in through her poke on foot before she has the mana or the terrain to threaten back.

edits.before: Taliyah's early kit is soft to your pressure — her Q needs worked ground she hasn't built up yet, and her E root has a long cooldown that leaves her exposed after every miss. From level 3 you can all-in through her poke and win most trades outright, since her low base stats and mana costs limit how much she can punish your approach. Push this advantage hard and don't let her freely build worked ground uncontested.
edits.after: Taliyah's early kit is soft to your pressure — her Q needs worked ground she hasn't built yet, and Unraveled Earth is a flat 14 seconds that only detonates on dashes, so an approach on foot walks straight through it. From level 3 you can all-in through her poke and win most trades outright, since her low base stats and mana costs limit how much she can punish you. Contest the worked ground she wants to kite on.

edits.before: Level 6 barely changes anything here — Weaver's Wall is a global-mobility and wave-clear tool, not a lane burst spike, so you keep the advantage straight through. Keep pressuring her whenever her root is down, and don't let her kite freely on worked ground; force fights close to your own combo range instead.
edits.after: Level 6 barely changes anything — Weaver's Wall is a mobility and wave-clear tool, not a burst spike, so you keep the advantage straight through. What does beat you is Seismic Shove throwing you into Unraveled Earth: being knocked through the mines stuns exactly like dashing through them, so fight where she has no minefield to shove you into.

edits.before: All-in aggressively whenever her E root is on cooldown
edits.after: All-in on foot so Unraveled Earth never gets to stun

edits.before: Land E roots to buy time to reposition before you close the gap
edits.after: Shove you into Unraveled Earth so the mines land the stun

notes: The dominant defect was calling Unraveled Earth a root. It is a slowing minefield that stuns only targets that DASH through it or are KNOCKED through it — which makes it the single sharpest anti-Akali tool in the game and it was never mentioned. Every affected string is corrected and the entry-on-foot / exit-on-dash rule is now stated in the cooldowns block, dosFull[0], phases[3] and phases[4]. Full-layer chart disagreed with content on all seven rows; flipped to Akali as one atomic group with the four rating changes. The kit's derived flags claim grounding on Threaded Volley and Seismic Shove; Riot's descriptions do not, so I asserted nothing about grounding — worth a data check. breakdown.wave, tradeGood, tradeBad and dosFull[1].d remain Akali-generic templates with male pronouns for Taliyah; I had no Taliyah-specific replacement that fit the length band without invention.
